extracted.intended_audience: professional communicators and IABC members (including PR practitioners, corporate communicators, and public information officers)
extracted.subtask_short: IABC Code of Ethics for communicators
extracted.subtask_description: A professional code of ethics setting standards and behavioral requirements for professional communicators (IABC members), covering legal, ethical, cultural, and professional-conduct principles plus enforcement and governance guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional communication is legal
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional communication is legal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Code is based on three interrelated principles; communicators' work must conform to laws governing their activities. Members are expected to obey laws and public policies and be sensitive to the spirit of laws (see related article).

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional communication is ethical
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional communication is ethical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethics are criteria for determining right and wrong agreed upon by members; members should refrain from taking part in undertakings they consider unethical and seek to improve competence through research and education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional communication is in good taste
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional communication is in good taste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding matters of taste requires sensitivity to cultural norms; communications should be sensitive to cultural values and beliefs and foster mutual understanding (see related article).

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage in communication that is legal, ethical and culturally sensitive
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage in communication that is not only legal but also ethical and sensitive to cultural values and beliefs;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizing the three principles, members will apply them in practice — combining legality, ethical judgment, and cultural sensitivity in all professional activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthful, accurate and fair communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage in truthful, accurate and fair communication that facilitates respect and mutual understanding;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicators must ensure their messages are factually correct, unbiased, and promote respect; this underpins obligations to disseminate accurate information and correct errors promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to ongoing competence and field knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Members will work to improve their individual competence and to increase the body of knowledge in the field with research and education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because conditions change, communicators should pursue professional development and contribute to the discipline through research and education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uphold credibility and dignity through honest, candid and timely communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional communicators uphold the credibility and dignity of their profession by practicing honest, candid and timely communication and by fostering the free flow of essential information in accord with the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicators should prioritize integrity, timeliness, and public-interest considerations when deciding what and how to communicate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disseminate accurate information and correct errors promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional communicators disseminate accurate information and promptly correct any erroneous communication for which they may be responsible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an error occurs, communicators are obligated to correct it promptly; accuracy is a continuous responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support free speech and open marketplace of ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional communicators understand and support the principles of free speech, freedom of assembly, and access to an open marketplace of ideas and act accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect for these principles should guide communicators' actions and choices about information access and expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be sensitive to cultural values and foster mutual understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional communicators are sensitive to cultural values and beliefs and engage in fair and balanced communication activities that foster and encourage mutual understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications should be balanced and fair, with attention to cultural norms to avoid offense and to build mutual respect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refrain from participating in unethical undertakings
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional communicators refrain from taking part in any undertaking which the communicator considers to be unethical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals must exercise personal ethical judgment and refuse involvement in activities they deem unethical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obey laws and public policies and correct violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional communicators obey laws and public policies governing their professional activities and are sensitive to the spirit of all laws and regulations and, should any law or public policy be violated, for whatever reason, act promptly to correct the situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal compliance is required; if violations occur (even inadvertently), communicators must act to remedy them promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give credit and identify sources and purposes of information
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional communicators give credit for unique expressions borrowed from others and identify the sources and purposes of all information disseminated to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribution and transparency about information sources and intentions are required to maintain trust and avoid plagiarism or misleading presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect confidentiality while complying with legal disclosure duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional communicators protect confidential information and, at the same time, comply with all legal requirements for the disclosure of information affecting the welfare of others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance confidentiality obligations with legal duties to disclose information when required for public welfare; confidentiality is important but not absolute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not misuse confidential information or represent conflicts without consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional communicators do not use confidential information gained as a result of professional activities for personal benefit and do not represent conflicting or competing interests without written consent of those involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid personal enrichment from privileged information and manage conflicts of interest transparently with written consent where representation of competing interests is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not accept undisclosed gifts or payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional communicators do not accept undisclosed gifts or payments for professional services from anyone other than a client or employer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepting undisclosed payments undermines independence and credibility; gifts and payments should be disclosed and limited to client/employer arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not guarantee results beyond practitioner control
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional communicators do not guarantee results that are beyond the power of the practitioner to deliver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be realistic and honest about likely outcomes; avoid promising specific results that cannot be assured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be honest with oneself and seek truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional communicators are honest not only with others but also, and most importantly, with themselves as individuals; for a professional communicator seeks the truth and speaks that truth first to the self.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-reflection and personal integrity are foundational; communicators should critically assess their motives and accuracy before presenting information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance fostered through education rather than punitive sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: IABC fosters compliance with its Code by engaging in global communication campaigns rather than through negative sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The association prefers education and promotion of the Code to enforce standards, using outreach and resources rather than immediate punitive action, though serious legal violations can lead to termination (see next metric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership termination for legal/judicial violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of IABC who are found guilty by an appropriate governmental agency or judicial body of violating laws and public policies governing their professional activities may have their membership terminated by the IABC executive board following procedures set forth in the association’s bylaws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serious legal violations can lead to termination following bylaw procedures; this is an enforcement backstop to the education-focused approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage wide communication and permit copying with attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: IABC encourages the widest possible communication about its Code... Permission is hereby granted to any individual or organization wishing to copy and incorporate all or part of the IABC Code into personal and corporate codes, with the understanding that appropriate credit be given to IABC in any publication of such codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations and individuals may reuse the Code or parts of it but should credit IABC when publishing derived codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish and educate about the Code; member acknowledgement required
rubrics_metrics.description: The IABC Code is published on the association’s web site... Communication World publishes periodic articles dealing with ethical issues. At least one session at the association’s annual conference is devoted to ethics... New and renewing members of IABC sign the following statement as part of their application: 'I have reviewed and understand the IABC Code of Ethics for Professional Communicators.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IABC integrates ethics into publications, conferences, and member onboarding; membership includes an explicit acknowledgment of understanding the Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics Committee functions and confidentiality limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The IABC Ethics Committee is composed of at least three accredited members... The functions of the Ethics Committee are to assist with professional development activities dealing with ethics and to offer advice and assistance to individual communicators regarding specific ethical situations. While discretion will be used in handling all inquiries about ethics, absolute confidentiality cannot be guaranteed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members may seek advice from the Ethics Committee for guidance and professional development; however, confidentiality is handled with discretion and not absolutely guaranteed. Contact information for World Headquarters is provided for further inquiries.
